articles.title: Show & Tel
articles.summary: The "Show & Tel" event, held on August 29th as "Slide and Equipment night," featured outdoor observing of sunspots and a rare red first quarter moon at Houge Park. Indoors, Chad Moore from Pinnacles National Monument discussed light pollution, followed by demonstrations of various astronomical equipment, including a Losmandy G-11 mount, a TL Systems equatorial platform, and a custom 8-inch Dobsonian telescope.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document presents the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activities calendar for October and September, detailing various events. It outlines star parties at Houge Park and Fremont Peak, general meetings featuring guest speakers on topics like meteorites and "Oxymoronic Astronomy," and a beginning astronomy class on CCD imaging. The calendar also includes notes on daylight saving time and Halloween, alongside contact information for the club.

articles.title: FPOA Starbecue
articles.summary: This article recounts Jane Houston's experience at the FPOA Starbecue event on August 22, an astronomy gathering featuring social interaction and observations. She attended with guests, including astronomer Dr. Chris McKay, and brought astronomy-themed baked goods. Highlights included daytime discussions, solar observations through various telescopes and filters, and witnessing collimation work on the 30-inch Challenger Telescope.

articles.title: Jay Freeman
articles.summary: This article discusses two primary topics: a simple yet effective test for assessing a telescope's baffling to detect internal light leaks, noting common issues in various telescope types like Newtonians, and a personal reflection on amateur astronomy. The author recounts delighting friends with a view of Saturn through a small refractor, which coincidentally marked their 10,000th logged observation since 1978 and mirrored their own beginnings in astronomy.

articles.title: Bill Arnett
articles.summary: This article details the September 1998 board meeting of an astronomical club, held on August 29. Key discussions included the ongoing work on the APD (Astronomical Programs Database), the club's liability insurance through the Astronomical League, and plans for observing the Leonids meteor shower. The board also discussed tree issues at Houge Park and sought volunteers for the Leonids event.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for October, highlighting Jupiter and Saturn as prime targets due to their excellent visibility and unique features, such as Jupiter's returning Great Red Spot and Saturn's more open rings. It also details the visibility of Mars, Uranus, and Neptune, while noting that Mercury, Venus, and Pluto will not be visible for most observers. Specific observing tips are given, including a close approach of Jupiter to a star and details to look for in Saturn's rings.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This October guide details lunar observing opportunities, highlighting features like Copernicus and Mare Humorum, and notes favorable third-quarter views despite unfavorable librations. It also mentions celestial events such as Jupiter conjunctions on the 3rd and 31st, and an Aldebaran occultation on the 9th. The article concludes with notes on the Moon's improving sky elevation and earlier dark skies making casual viewing easier, along with the year's greatest apogee on October 21st.

articles.title: Meteor Watch
articles.summary: This 'Meteor Watch' article details two meteor showers for observation in October 1998: the Draconids and the Orionids. The Draconids, active around October 8-10 and linked to comet 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, hold a slight possibility of a meteor storm despite an interfering waning gibbous moon. The Orionids, originating from Halley's Comet, will peak between October 17-25 under excellent dark sky conditions thanks to a new moon, with hourly rates averaging around 20 meteors.

articles.title: Editor's Extras
articles.summary: This 'Editor's Extras' column provides updates on several club members and upcoming events. Paul Barton is recovering from a stroke, while active new member Jane Houston's relationship with Morris Jones is highlighted. The article also mentions Jack Zeiders' father's passing, announces a highly anticipated CCD Astronomy class by Kevin Medlock, and warns of a potential delay in the next Ephemeris publication.

articles.title: Starbecue, continued from Page One
articles.summary: This article details a vibrant 'Starbecue' astronomy event, highlighting communal activities such as shared food, social interaction, and extensive telescope viewing, including a 30-inch Challenger scope. The Amateur Astronomers Association of Northern California (AANC) presented awards to notable figures like Dr. Chris McKay (Professional Astronomer), Steve Overholt (Amateur Astronomer), Tectron Telescopes (Commercial), and SETI (Special Award). The successful gathering featured widespread stargazing and educational engagement for children, creating a memorable night for all attendees.

articles.title: From Page One
articles.summary: The article reports on an astronomical gathering where members showcased various equipment, including custom telescopes like a 6-inch newt, a 55mm refractor, and a work-in-progress alt/az goto mount. Presentations featured a remarkable solar eclipse photo, educational star/constellation slides for beginner classes, and an eclipse video. The event concluded with an outdoor observing session focused on the Moon and Jupiter, and also noted a vintage Questar telescope for sale.

articles.title: Activities Through Other Clubs
articles.summary: This article details astronomical activities and events organized by other clubs, encouraging SJAA members to participate. TAC reserves the Montebello site for Wednesday night observing, requiring a permit holder and checking their webpage for updates. PAS offers public viewing at Foothill Observatory on clear Friday evenings and solar viewing on Saturday mornings, in addition to their scheduled general and board meetings in October and November.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed celestial calendar for October 1998, outlining lunar phases with their times, rise, transit, and set data. It also includes comprehensive ephemeris data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, detailing their positions, magnitudes, and distances. Furthermore, it offers information on solar times, astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and highlights the 'Darkest Saturday Night' for optimal observing.

articles.title: Don Machholz
articles.summary: This article discusses recent comet activity, highlighting the visual discovery of Comet Williams by Peter Williams in Australia on August 10, and Comet C/1998 Q1 by the LINEAR project. It provides details on Comet Williams' discovery, retrograde orbit, and future visibility, along with an update on Periodic Comet Tempel 1's elongated nucleus based on Hubble Space Telescope observations. The piece also notes Williams' qualification for the Edgar Wilson Award and statistics on Southern Hemisphere comet discoverers.

articles.title: Ephemerides - Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: The document provides ephemerides for four comets—C/1997 J2, C/1998 P1, 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, and C/1998 M5—specified for Epoch 2000, 0h UTC. For each comet, tables detail their Right Ascension, Declination, elongation, sky visibility, and apparent magnitude across dates from early October to early November. This data is critical for astronomers and observers to track these celestial objects.

articles.title: Orbital Elements -- Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document presents a table of orbital elements for four celestial objects, including Giacobini-Zinner and LINEAR, all referenced to Epoch 2000.0. It details parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period. The data is part of an SJAA Ephemeris dated October 1998.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors, including the President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and several Directors. Each individual's name is provided along with a contact phone number.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document outlines the key staff and contact information for various roles and programs within an organization, likely related to an 'Ephemeris' publication or group. It lists contacts for editorial, circulation, printing, and specific initiatives such as a Mentoring Program, Observational Astronomy, an Observatory Committee, School Star Parties, and a Telescope Loaner Program. The list also includes the contact for the organization's web page.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: This article encourages members to submit articles for publication in the SJAA Ephemeris. Submissions should be sent via email to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com.

articles.title: Finding Fremont Peak
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to Fremont Peak State Park, located south of San Juan Bautista. It outlines the route from Hwy 101, including specific highway numbers, mileage, turns, and notes about road jogs and the park's entrance fee.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: This article provides an update on the Telescope Loaner Program, which is a service exclusively available to members of the SJAA. Members interested in utilizing this program are directed to contact Mike Koop at the provided phone number.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists astronomical telescopes currently on loan, detailing each scope's description, the borrower, and its due date. It also informs potential borrowers that they can be placed on a waiting list for scopes once they become available.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes that currently have extended loan periods. Individuals interested in borrowing one of these scopes can contact the organization to arrange a transfer with the current borrower. The list includes details such as scope description, current borrower, and due date for each extended loan item.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: This document lists various telescopes (Newtonian, Refractor, Dobsonian) that are available for immediate loan to members of the SJAA. These scopes are stored at other members' homes, and interested individuals should contact Mike Koop to arrange a pickup at an SJAA event.

articles.title: Waiting List
articles.summary: This brief notice lists two items currently on a waiting list: a C8 telescope for astrophotography (Alexander Koczur) and a large Dobsonian telescope (George Cooper). It also includes a call for members with available space to store telescopes, asking them to contact Mike Koop.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly throughout the year. The document also provides instructions for subscribing to or unsubscribing from the SJAA mailing list and is dated October 1998.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing how to apply for or renew membership. It lists membership fees ($15 for standard, $6 for junior) and an optional subscription to Sky & Telescope for an additional $27. Instructions are provided for submitting the form and payment via mail to the treasurer or in person at an SJAA meeting.
